original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Answer #3451's first open question for present-head flag 1 (X0 -> Y7, basis head 232): price changed schedules that co-host the head at Y7's delivering update (2797, the only Y7 update carrying X0) while X0 still hosts it and is live. Build two explicit splices of the published #1991 word, run the published p104-native-channel validate() on each with six newly lowered native edges, and give the exact before/after bill (events, ADDs, transport occurrences, rank mass, paid H_r profile, native edges, per-register surcharge). Add the matching obstruction: with zero added non-private rank mass no order-preserving repair co-hosts at any of Y7's six updates, and no relocation of the delivering ADD to any of 868 of its 1,115 legal slots does either; by parity the surcharge floor there is 2.
scope_change_reason: #3451 proves the published word never co-hosts flag 1's basis head at a target update and leaves pricing a repair open; #3508 priced the analogous flag-43 repair at zero added cost. This package cites #3451 and #3508 without re-deriving them, and shows that flag 1 differs: its forced set is blocked at zero mass, so the repair costs two rank units.
bottleneck_link: Unlike flag 43, the present-head obstruction on flag 1 is not a pure scheduling artefact: every order-preserving co-hosting repair needs at least two added rank units, and two natively validated repairs reach exactly that floor (R0 order-preserving +1 event/+1 transport/+2 rank; R1 relocated, 0 events/0 transports/+2 rank). Whether a zero-mass relocation exists after 3366 is left open. This does not supply I-G/2, a side correction or a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after one flag (1): one order-preserving repair R0 and one relocation R1, both natively validated and billed, plus the head closure and exact least-frame zero-mass sweep for every Y7 update and every relocation slot of the delivering ADD. Do not touch flags 0, 9 or 43, recompute relay coefficients beyond the X0 entry delivered into Y7, or build a side correction.
evidence: Only 2797 (Y7 += D17/4, chart [95,486]) carries X0 into Y7 (-1/2, its final coefficient); D17's row is written only at 2497 and 3613 and Y7 is never read. R0 retargets 2795 (D17 [486]->[95,486,232], rank 2), 2796 (Y7 [95]->[95,486,232], rank 2), relabels the 2797 chart to [95,486,232], inserts D17 [95,486,232]->[95,486] (rank 1) after it, and retargets 3473 (Y7 -> final, rank 5). R1 moves Y7's 2796/2797/3473 into D17's full window after 3612: Y7 [95]->FULL (rank 8), the ADD in FULL, Y7 FULL->final (rank 1). The published check_native.validate() passes on both (742 and 741 native edges, 208 adapters, 280 framed rows, 72 dirty helpers restored); independent replay gives 280/280 rows equal. Bill: R0 4059 events, 2624 ADDs, 1411 transports, rank mass 2370, profile delta -H1+2H2+H5-H6, +2 on D17; R1 4058 events, 2624 ADDs, 1410 transports, rank mass 2370, delta H8-H6, +2 on Y7; C untouched. Obstruction: all 280 non-private registers sit at their rank floor; the #3508 head closure blocks all six Y7 updates (56,56,56,56,23,14 excluded finals, first Y8); the exact least-frame sweep with C relaxed is infeasible for all six order-preserving updates and for 868/1115 relocation slots (every slot before Y103's read at 3366), feasible for the remaining 247. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-added-mass co-hosting repair with flag 1's delivering ADD relocated after 3366?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The relaxed least-frame sweep allows it; a construction would make flag 1's present-head obstruction a pure scheduling artefact like flag 43's, while a proof of impossibility would make the +2 floor global over relocations.
open_questions.first_step: Search for frames that place D17's 3182-3188 and 3362-3366 read charts inside final(Y7) by lowering the five partner targets' frames, keeping X sources' initial frames and the private register's charts fixed.
open_questions.blocked_by: The direct intersection with final(Y7) cascades to 208 registers and needs 56 source initial frames inside final(Y7); no alternative construction is attempted here.

open_questions.question: Which +2 repair is cheaper under the repository's actual per-rank weights?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 costs a+2b and R1 costs 2b under affine prices, but R0's delta -H1+2H2+H5-H6 turns negative for steep convex prices (H=r^2 gives -4).
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate both deltas under the per-rank weights used by the selected channel bill.

open_questions.question: Does flag 9 (#3443) follow flag 1's pattern (blocked at zero mass, +2 at the floor) or flag 43's (zero-cost repair)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the present-head obstruction is uniformly priced or split by flag.
open_questions.first_step: Run this package's head closure and least-frame sweep on flag 9's target with head 196 in a separate package citing #3443, keeping its generator-only source-drop limit.
open_questions.blocked_by: Flag 9 is the subject of open #3443 and is not touched here.
